llm.summary: The skill's purpose (a runtime security plugin) is plausible and largely consistent with its instructions, but it instructs automatic registration with a remote 'Core' service and creation/storage/sharing of API keys without explaining what agent data will be sent, which is a privacy/credential-proportionality concern you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (runtime security plugin) align with the instructions: installing an OpenClaw plugin and using a remote 'Core' service to perform detections is coherent for a security product.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md tells the agent/user to install the plugin via 'openclaw plugins install' and states that all detection is performed by a remote 'Core'. It also describes automatic registration and saving of credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard. The document does not clearly specify what prompts/files/metadata will be uploaded to Core, how long data is retained, or whether sensitive content is excluded—so the instructions imply remote transmission of potentially sensitive data without explicit consent/limits.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill and includes no install spec. It tells the user to run 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard', which will download and install code at runtime outside this skill bundle. Because the bundle contains no code, the scan couldn't inspect the plugin that the install command fetches — you should review the plugin source or package before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, but advertises auto-registration that creates an API key stored under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard and features that show the API key (/og_status). That implicit creation and local storage of credentials — plus account/agent claiming that shares quotas across machines — is disproportionate to a purely local, offline protector and raises credential-sharing and privacy concerns. No details are given about key scopes or revocation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). However, the onboarding flow's auto-registration and cross-machine account/quota model mean the plugin will persist credentials on disk and may be invoked autonomously by agents. Autonomous invocation is normal for skills, but combined with opaque remote processing and shared account keys it increases the blast radius if the remote service or keys are compromised.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing, consider the following:
- This SKILL.md is only instructions; the real plugin will be fetched by 'openclaw plugins install'. Inspect the plugin's source code and release artifacts (the GitHub link is provided) before running the install.
- MoltGuard says detection is performed by a remote 'Core' service and that it auto-registers and stores an API key under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard. Ask: what exactly is sent to Core (prompts, files, metadata), how long is it retained, who can access it, and is there a privacy policy or DPA?
- If your agent will process sensitive data (PII, credentials, internal documents), test the plugin in a sandbox or on non-sensitive data first. Confirm there is an option to run detection locally or to opt out of uploading content.
- Confirm how to revoke or rotate the generated API key and how to completely uninstall the plugin (the doc suggests rm -rf but consider whether the openclaw registry has an uninstall command and whether other residual data exists).
- Be cautious about the 'claim agent' workflow that shares quotas across machines — only use it if you trust the account and understand implications of sharing an API key/Agent ID across hosts.
- If you need higher assurance, request details about data flows and retention from the vendor or install the plugin only after reviewing its published code and release artifacts.
